title: Lusin's theorem for an a.e. strongly measurable map, keeping an a.e. property (parent steps 1–2; the closed set F of Simon Ch. 3, proof of 1.6, (4))
statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and let Y be a pseudo-metrizable, second-countable topological space. Let μ be a measure on ℝ^P (Borel σ-algebra), A ⊆ ℝ^P a Borel set with μ(A) < ∞, f : ℝ^P → Y a map that is almost everywhere strongly measurable with respect to μ⌞A, and p a property of points of ℝ^P that holds μ⌞A-almost everywhere. Then for every η ∈ (0, ∞] (η ≠ 0) there is a compact set K ⊆ A with μ(A ∖ K) < η such that p(x) holds for every x ∈ K and f is continuous on K.
lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) {Y : Type} [TopologicalSpace Y] [TopologicalSpace.PseudoMetrizableSpace Y] [SecondCountableTopology Y] (μ : Measure (Euclid P)) (A : Set (Euclid P)) (f : Euclid P → Y) (p : Euclid P → Prop), MeasurableSet A → μ A ≠ ∞ → AEStronglyMeasurable f (μ.restrict A) → (∀ᵐ x ∂(μ.restrict A), p x) → ∀ η : ℝ≥0∞, η ≠ 0 → ∃ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K ∧ K ⊆ A ∧ μ (A \ K) < η ∧ (∀ x ∈ K, p x) ∧ ContinuousOn f K
